_meta.purpose: UK source catalogue (25 entries) · tight-scope relaunch after original agent timed out
_meta.governance_rule: Sources only. Never invent. Mark unverified honestly.
_meta.verification_note: 5 of 25 sources confirmed via targeted WebSearch (Approved Document K, BS 5395-1, BWF Stair Scheme, Scottish Technical Handbook April 2026, TRADA publications). Remaining 20 are widely-recognised UK trade/regulatory references marked requires_manual_verification per governance rule 2/3.

sources.source_name: Approved Document K — Protection from falling, collision and impact
sources.organisation: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG) / Department for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities (England)
sources.document_title: The Building Regulations 2010 — Approved Document K: Protection from falling, collision and impact (2013 edition incorporating 2013 amendments)
sources.citation_format: HM Government (2013) Approved Document K: Protection from falling, collision and impact. The Building Regulations 2010. London: MHCLG.
sources.notes: Statutory guidance for England. Sections K1 (stairs, ladders, ramps) and K2 (protection from falling) are the primary staircase references. Verified via WebSearch.

sources.source_name: Approved Document B — Fire safety (Volume 1: Dwellings)
sources.organisation: MHCLG / Department for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities (England)
sources.document_title: The Building Regulations 2010 — Approved Document B: Fire safety, Volume 1 — Dwellings (2019 edition incorporating 2020 and 2022 amendments)
sources.citation_format: HM Government (2019) Approved Document B: Fire safety, Volume 1 — Dwellings. The Building Regulations 2010. London: MHCLG.
sources.notes: Governs means of escape stairs, protected stair enclosures, fire door protection to staircases. URL is the landing page; not directly re-verified this session.

sources.source_name: Approved Document B — Fire safety (Volume 2: Buildings other than dwellings)
sources.organisation: MHCLG / Department for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities (England)
sources.document_title: The Building Regulations 2010 — Approved Document B: Fire safety, Volume 2 — Buildings other than dwellings
sources.citation_format: HM Government (2019) Approved Document B: Fire safety, Volume 2 — Buildings other than dwellings. London: MHCLG.
sources.notes: Governs non-domestic stair widths, escape capacities, protected shafts. Landing page not re-verified this session.

sources.source_name: Approved Document M — Access to and use of buildings (Volume 1: Dwellings)
sources.organisation: MHCLG / Department for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities (England)
sources.document_title: The Building Regulations 2010 — Approved Document M: Access to and use of buildings, Volume 1 — Dwellings
sources.citation_format: HM Government (2015) Approved Document M: Access to and use of buildings, Volume 1 — Dwellings. London: MHCLG.
sources.notes: Categories M4(1)/M4(2)/M4(3) dwellings — accessible stair provision. Landing page not re-verified this session.

sources.source_name: Approved Document E — Resistance to the passage of sound
sources.organisation: MHCLG / Department for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities (England)
sources.document_title: The Building Regulations 2010 — Approved Document E: Resistance to the passage of sound
sources.citation_format: HM Government (2003) Approved Document E: Resistance to the passage of sound. London: MHCLG.
sources.notes: Relevant to staircases within party wall/floor constructions and flat conversions. Landing page not re-verified this session.

sources.source_name: Scottish Building Standards — Technical Handbook (Domestic), April 2026
sources.document_title: Building Standards Technical Handbook — Domestic (April 2026 edition), Section 4: Safety
sources.citation_format: Scottish Government (2026) Building Standards Technical Handbook — Domestic, April 2026 edition. Edinburgh: Building Standards Division.
sources.notes: Section 4.3 covers stairs and ramps. Section 4 revised in April 2026 update. Verified via WebSearch.

sources.source_name: Northern Ireland Technical Booklet H — Stairs, ramps, guarding and protection from impact
sources.organisation: Department of Finance (Northern Ireland) — Building Regulations Branch
sources.document_title: Technical Booklet H: Stairs, ramps, guarding and protection from impact (Building Regulations (Northern Ireland))
sources.citation_format: Department of Finance NI (2012) Technical Booklet H: Stairs, ramps, guarding and protection from impact. Belfast: Building Regulations Branch.
sources.notes: NI equivalent of Approved Document K. URL left null — not verified this session; typically hosted on finance-ni.gov.uk building regulations pages.

sources.source_name: Republic of Ireland Technical Guidance Document K — Stairways, Ladders, Ramps and Guards
sources.organisation: Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage (Ireland)
sources.document_title: Technical Guidance Document K — Stairways, Ladders, Ramps and Guards
sources.citation_format: Government of Ireland (2014) Technical Guidance Document K — Stairways, Ladders, Ramps and Guards. Building Regulations. Dublin: DHLGH.
sources.notes: Republic of Ireland equivalent to Approved Document K — included as cross-border reference for UK trade operating in NI/ROI. URL not verified this session.

sources.source_name: BS 5395-1:2010 — Stairs. Code of practice for the design of stairs with straight flights and winders
sources.document_title: BS 5395-1:2010 Stairs — Part 1: Code of practice for the design of stairs with straight flights and winders
sources.citation_format: BSI (2010) BS 5395-1:2010 Stairs — Part 1: Code of practice for the design of stairs with straight flights and winders. London: British Standards Institution.
sources.notes: Primary UK code of practice for domestic and general straight-flight stair design. Supersedes BS 5395-1:2000. 42 pages. Verified via WebSearch.

sources.source_name: BS 5395-2:1984 — Stairs. Code of practice for the design of helical and spiral stairs
sources.document_title: BS 5395-2:1984 Stairs, ladders and walkways — Part 2: Code of practice for the design of helical and spiral stairs
sources.citation_format: BSI (1984) BS 5395-2:1984 Stairs — Part 2: Code of practice for the design of helical and spiral stairs. London: British Standards Institution.
sources.notes: Companion to BS 5395-1 covering helical/spiral geometry. Long-standing edition still current at last check. URL not verified this session.

sources.source_name: BS 5395-3:1985 — Stairs. Code of practice for the design of industrial type stairs, permanent ladders and walkways
sources.document_title: BS 5395-3:1985 Stairs — Part 3: Code of practice for the design of industrial type stairs, permanent ladders and walkways
sources.citation_format: BSI (1985) BS 5395-3:1985 Stairs — Part 3: Code of practice for the design of industrial type stairs, permanent ladders and walkways. London: British Standards Institution.
sources.notes: Applies to industrial stairs outside residential scope. Note BS 4592-0 addresses industrial flooring/stair treads. URL not verified this session.

sources.source_name: BS EN 14076:2013 — Timber stairs. Terminology
sources.document_title: BS EN 14076:2013 Timber stairs — Terminology
sources.citation_format: BSI (2013) BS EN 14076:2013 Timber stairs — Terminology. London: British Standards Institution.
sources.notes: Canonical terminology reference — defines tread, riser, string, newel, winder, bullnose etc. across EU member states. URL not verified this session.

sources.source_name: BS 585-1:1989 — Wood stairs. Specification for stairs with closed risers for domestic use, including straight and winder flights and quarter or half landings
sources.document_title: BS 585-1:1989 Wood stairs — Part 1: Specification for stairs with closed risers for domestic use, including straight and winder flights and quarter or half landings
sources.citation_format: BSI (1989) BS 585-1:1989 Wood stairs — Part 1: Specification for stairs with closed risers for domestic use. London: British Standards Institution.
sources.notes: Older UK spec for timber domestic stairs — largely superseded by BS 5395-1/BS EN 14076 but still cited by heritage joinery and legacy building surveys. URL not verified this session.

sources.source_name: TRADA Wood Information Sheets — timber stair guidance series
sources.document_title: Wood Information Sheets (WIS) series covering stair specification, timber species selection and joinery details
sources.publication_date: Series (ongoing until BM TRADA publishing closure 2024-12-31)
sources.citation_format: TRADA (various) Wood Information Sheets series. High Wycombe: TRADA Technology.
sources.notes: TRADA publishes Timber annual and WIS series — 2016 annual included staircase specification article. BM TRADA publishing operation closed 31 Dec 2024; back catalogue still accessible via TRADA members. URL is TRADA landing page.

sources.source_name: TRADA — Timber (annual publication)
sources.document_title: Timber — TRADA annual publication (various years, includes staircase specification articles)
sources.publication_date: Annual (2016 edition contains staircase specification content)
sources.citation_format: TRADA (2016) Timber 2016. High Wycombe: TRADA Technology.
sources.notes: Annual featuring stair specification article and case studies. Free web preview via Issuu. URL is Issuu landing for 2016 edition.

sources.source_name: BWF Stair Scheme — Design Guide 1: Domestic Timber Stairs
sources.document_title: BWF Stair Scheme Design Guide 1 — Domestic Timber Stairs
sources.publication_date: Latest revision 2025 (multiple editions since scheme launch)
sources.citation_format: British Woodworking Federation (2025) BWF Stair Scheme Design Guide 1 — Domestic Timber Stairs. London: BWF.
sources.notes: Primary manufacturer-facing UK design guide for domestic timber stairs. BWF Stair Scheme represents ~70% of UK timber stair market. Verified via WebSearch.

sources.source_name: BWF Stair Scheme — Design Guide 2: Common Stairs
sources.document_title: BWF Stair Scheme Design Guide 2 — Common Stairs (multi-occupancy)
sources.citation_format: British Woodworking Federation (2017) BWF Stair Scheme Design Guide 2 — Common Stairs. London: BWF.
sources.notes: Common stairs in flats/HMOs including fire-protected common stairs. Verified via WebSearch (URL surfaced in same query as Design Guide 1).

sources.source_name: Historic England — Traditional Windows and Stairs technical guidance
sources.document_title: Historic England technical advice notes on traditional staircases, joinery repair and heritage conservation
sources.citation_format: Historic England (various) Technical Advice — traditional joinery and staircase conservation. Swindon: Historic England.
sources.notes: Guidance for conservation of Georgian/Victorian/Edwardian staircases in listed buildings. Landing page URL — specific stair advice notes not individually verified this session.

sources.source_name: Historic Environment Scotland — Short Guide series (traditional joinery and stairs)
sources.document_title: HES Short Guide series covering traditional joinery, stair repair and tenement conservation
sources.citation_format: Historic Environment Scotland (various) Short Guide series. Edinburgh: HES.
sources.notes: Scottish heritage counterpart to Historic England guidance — particularly relevant for Edinburgh/Glasgow tenement common stairs. Landing page URL.

sources.source_name: SPAB — Society for the Protection of Ancient Buildings technical advice
sources.organisation: SPAB (Society for the Protection of Ancient Buildings)
sources.document_title: SPAB Technical Q&A and Advice Notes covering timber stair repair, historic joinery and traditional carpentry
sources.citation_format: SPAB (various) Technical Advice. London: Society for the Protection of Ancient Buildings.
sources.notes: Independent charity founded 1877 — authoritative on minimum-intervention repair of historic timber staircases. Landing page URL.

sources.source_name: City & Guilds Level 2 & Level 3 Diploma in Site Carpentry / Bench Joinery (6706 / 6570)
sources.document_title: City & Guilds Diploma in Site Carpentry (Level 2 6706-22) and Bench Joinery (Level 2/3), including stair construction units
sources.citation_format: City & Guilds (current) Level 2/3 Diploma in Site Carpentry and Architectural Joinery (6706). London: City & Guilds.
sources.notes: Includes stair construction, installation and setting-out units. Landing page URL — specification document not individually re-verified this session.

sources.source_name: NVQ Level 2/3 Wood Occupations (Construction) — CSkills Awards / NOCN
sources.document_title: NVQ Diploma Level 2/3 in Wood Occupations (Construction) — Bench Joinery / Site Carpentry pathways
sources.citation_format: CSkills Awards / NOCN (current) NVQ Diploma in Wood Occupations, Levels 2 and 3. Peterborough: NOCN.
sources.notes: On-site assessment route sitting alongside City & Guilds — required for CSCS Blue/Gold Skilled Worker cards in carpentry/joinery. URL not verified this session — specifications move between awarding organisations.

sources.source_name: PVA adhesive datasheet category — Class D3/D4 wood adhesives (EN 204)
sources.organisation: Adhesive manufacturer datasheets aligned to BS EN 204:2016
sources.document_title: Wood adhesive manufacturer technical datasheets — D3/D4 classification per BS EN 204
sources.citation_format: Various manufacturers (current) D3/D4 PVA wood adhesive technical datasheets per BS EN 204:2016. [Manufacturer, Location].
sources.notes: Category-level source per governance rule (no specific product). Covers Titebond, Everbuild, Bostik, Franklin International, Purbond etc. — used for treads-to-strings, riser-to-tread, wedge bonding. URL null because category not single-product.

sources.source_name: Screw and mechanical fixing datasheet category — timber-to-timber (BS EN 14592)
sources.organisation: Fastener manufacturer datasheets aligned to BS EN 14592
sources.document_title: Structural and joinery screw/dowel technical datasheets — timber fasteners per BS EN 14592
sources.citation_format: Various manufacturers (current) Timber fastener technical datasheets per BS EN 14592. [Manufacturer, Location].
sources.notes: Category-level source per governance rule. Covers Rothoblaas, Simpson Strong-Tie, Spax, Reisser, Rawlplug etc. — screws through riser to tread underside, newel-post fixings, handrail bracket fixings. URL null because category not single-product.

sources.source_name: HSE — Health and Safety Executive guidance on stairs, falls and workplace transport
sources.document_title: HSE guidance including Workplace (Health, Safety and Welfare) Regulations 1992 ACOP L24 and slips/trips/falls guidance (INDG225 etc.)
sources.citation_format: HSE (2013) L24 Workplace health, safety and welfare — Workplace (Health, Safety and Welfare) Regulations 1992, Approved Code of Practice and guidance. Sudbury: HSE Books.
sources.notes: L24 ACOP covers workplace stair maintenance, handrail provision and slip resistance. Companion HSE slips/trips resources apply to stair nosings. URL is standard HSE L24 path — not re-verified this session.
